styles.name: Pixel Art
styles.description: Chunky digital mascot built from deliberate pixel clusters, a simple dark outline and a compact color ramp.

instructions.materials: Opaque digital pixel clusters with no simulated physical surface.
instructions.forms: Build a chunky silhouette from squat interlocking blocks and readable face clusters.
instructions.linework: Use a simple dark contour with deliberate stair steps and consistent corner rules.
instructions.shading: Place flat cel-shadow clusters beneath forms; avoid interpolated lighting between color steps.
instructions.palette: Limit each material to a small stable ramp with clearly separated values.
instructions.texture: Keep visible stepped edges and purposeful pixel clusters rather than random grain.
instructions.rendering: Construct the entire isolated mascot on one consistent logical pixel grid.

negative_constraints: Avoid softened pixel edges, fractional-grid outlines or isolated noise pixels.
Do not replace the chunky face with high-resolution painted anatomy.
use_cases: Codex pets with strongly readable expressions
Small game sprites and grid-oriented assets
limitations: Non-integer resizing can introduce uneven pixel widths and destroy the intended contour rhythm.

compatibility.scaling: Use a consistent logical pixel grid and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement inside the existing profile cells; preserve whole pixel clusters.
notes: Choose a chroma key outside every palette ramp; retain hard opaque boundary pixels when removing it.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: 8-Bit Sprite
styles.description: Very compact tile-era sprite language using broad square features, sparse color clusters and emphatic poses.

instructions.materials: Use opaque square pixels as the only mark-making unit.
instructions.forms: Reduce limbs, muzzle and props to a few broad tile-like masses.
instructions.linework: Describe contours with short straight runs and simple one-step corners.
instructions.shading: Use one shadow color per material and omit reflected-light modeling.
instructions.palette: Keep a small shared set of colors with large value gaps between neighbors.
instructions.texture: Let large unbroken pixel patches dominate, with almost no internal dithering.
instructions.rendering: Draw an isolated sprite whose pose is legible before any interior detail is added.

negative_constraints: Avoid smooth gradients or hundreds of one-pixel accent colors.
Do not add display hardware, score text or a game-level backdrop.
limitations: Tiny facial markings and complicated accessories need deliberate simplification to remain distinct.

compatibility.scaling: Use a consistent logical pixel grid and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement inside the existing profile cells; preserve whole pixel clusters.
notes: Keep the source pixel pitch constant across all rows; reposition complete clusters instead of resampling each pose independently.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: 16-Bit Sprite
styles.description: Rounded pixel character with controlled color ramps, selective outlines and small clustered highlights.

instructions.materials: Treat the character as richly colored opaque sprite pixels rather than a filtered painting.
instructions.forms: Shape rounded limbs and expressive heads through planned multi-pixel arcs.
instructions.linework: Use selective dark outlines on shadow sides and lighter contour colors near highlights.
instructions.shading: Model each volume with two or three broad stepped shade bands.
instructions.palette: Give each material a short coordinated ramp with a warm light and cooler shadow.
instructions.texture: Add a few compact highlight clusters while leaving large surfaces uncluttered.
instructions.rendering: Render the isolated pose with crisp cluster boundaries and consistent implied upper-side lighting.

negative_constraints: Avoid blurred edges or continuous photographic light falloff.
Do not scatter single-pixel sparkle noise across moving surfaces.
limitations: Additional shading must not crowd small faces or reduce separation between neighboring limbs.

compatibility.scaling: Use a consistent logical pixel grid and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement inside the existing profile cells; preserve whole pixel clusters.
notes: Preserve selective outline colors during extraction; a pale contour pixel is artwork, not necessarily background spill.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: 32-Bit Sprite
styles.description: Detailed pre-rendered sprite language with dense but controlled pixel shading and carefully sampled curved volumes.

instructions.materials: Suggest sculpted surfaces represented by deliberately sampled opaque color pixels.
instructions.forms: Use compact volumetric forms with round joints and broad readable planes.
instructions.linework: Keep a crisp sampled perimeter with subdued colored edge pixels rather than a heavy outline.
instructions.shading: Build smooth-looking volume from several ordered pixel shade bands and clustered highlights.
instructions.palette: Use richer material ramps while keeping the approved hue families stable.
instructions.texture: Allow restrained interior dithering in large shade transitions, never at facial landmarks.
instructions.rendering: Render a convincing toy-like volume as a crisp isolated sprite without applying a blur filter.

negative_constraints: Avoid noisy photo reduction, compression artifacts or random edge antialias colors.
Do not turn subtle surface modeling into moving specular glitter.
limitations: The richer shading needs actual-size review because fine ramps can collapse into muddy patches.

compatibility.scaling: Use a consistent logical pixel grid and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement inside the existing profile cells; preserve whole pixel clusters.
notes: Approve a fixed light direction and shade ramp in the base so darker edge samples remain stable during animation.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: Isometric Pixel Art
styles.description: Axonometric pixel mascot with a consistent diagonal grid, readable top planes and stair-stepped volume.

instructions.materials: Use clean opaque pixel planes with a crafted game-object finish.
instructions.forms: Construct the body from compact isometric masses with visible top and side planes.
instructions.linework: Follow consistent two-across one-up diagonal stair steps on major receding edges.
instructions.shading: Shade top, near side and far side as three distinct planar values.
instructions.palette: Assign a small material ramp to each approved color with strong plane separation.
instructions.texture: Keep plane interiors mostly solid; use small seams only where the identity needs them.
instructions.rendering: Hold the isometric viewing angle constant while animating the isolated character within each slot.

negative_constraints: Avoid a perspective floor, tile platform or cast shadow beneath the mascot.
Do not change camera angle or diagonal grid between animation states.
limitations: Front-facing expressions and direction changes must be adapted to the fixed axonometric camera.

compatibility.scaling: Use a consistent logical pixel grid and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement inside the existing profile cells; preserve whole pixel clusters.
notes: Do not rotate a finished raster to obtain new views; draw each approved view on the same isometric grid.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: Dithered Pixel Art
styles.description: Pixel forms shaded with intentional repeating dither patterns instead of extra intermediate colors.

instructions.materials: Use opaque pixel ink with patterned mixtures standing in for intermediate tones.
instructions.forms: Start from broad solid body masses that can hold several readable dither patches.
instructions.linework: Maintain a clean stepped contour free from checkerboard holes at the perimeter.
instructions.shading: Transition between light and shade using fixed checker or diagonal dither motifs.
instructions.palette: Use a compact set of approved colors whose paired mixtures remain visibly distinct.
instructions.texture: Place dither patches inside larger planes and anchor the pattern to each body part.
instructions.rendering: Render isolated pixel artwork with patterned shade transitions and an undithered readable face.

negative_constraints: Avoid randomly changing dither seeds, shimmering patterns or transparent speckles.
Do not cover tiny eyes, mouth or identity markings with dense checkerboard texture.
limitations: Dither patterns may shimmer when scaled fractionally or moved without regard to the logical pixel grid.

compatibility.scaling: Use a consistent logical pixel grid and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement inside the existing profile cells; preserve whole pixel clusters.
notes: Lock the chosen dither motif and its body-relative origin in the approved base; review motion for texture crawl.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: Voxel Sculpture
styles.description: A compact character assembled from visible cubic units with lit planar faces and block-stepped contours.

instructions.materials: Build the mascot from solid matte cubic units with gently lit faces.
instructions.forms: Stack cubes into a squat recognizable body, stepped cheeks and blocky articulated limbs.
instructions.linework: Let cube boundaries and silhouette steps define edges instead of drawn ink.
instructions.shading: Separate top and side faces with flat directional lighting and small contact occlusion.
instructions.palette: Reuse a few body colors, each with consistent light and dark face values.
instructions.texture: Show selected block seams on broad surfaces without outlining every hidden cube.
instructions.rendering: Render the isolated cubic construction at a consistent three-quarter camera and scale.

negative_constraints: Avoid smoothing the cubes into rounded clay or covering them with photo textures.
Do not add a terrain base, floating cubes or ambient floor shadow.
limitations: Thin limbs may require larger block groupings; tiny voxel details can disappear at pet size.

compatibility.scaling: Render with sufficient source detail, then downsample once with the recommended filter into the existing profile cells; inspect the final silhouette at actual size.
notes: Antialias the rendered outer contour lightly while preserving planar cube faces; voxel geometry does not imply a mandatory pixel-art raster grid.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: Retro Handheld Sprite
styles.description: Portable-game sprite with soft-looking color relationships, coarse clusters and especially compact limb gestures.

instructions.materials: Represent colored LCD sprite pixels as opaque patches without drawing a screen enclosure.
instructions.forms: Favor a large head, short limbs and broad gestures designed for a tiny display.
instructions.linework: Use a dark colored perimeter with blunt corners and few isolated protrusions.
instructions.shading: Add only one compact shadow patch and one highlight patch to each large form.
instructions.palette: Favor restrained portable-display colors while retaining explicit identity and brand hues.
instructions.texture: Keep a coarse consistent pixel pitch with quiet solid interiors and minimal surface detail.
instructions.rendering: Produce an isolated color-handheld sprite, making pose changes through clusters rather than fine anatomy.

negative_constraints: Avoid a bezel, battery icon, game UI or tinted rectangular screen background.
Do not replace broad clusters with high-detail console rendering.
limitations: Approved markings must be simplified if they are thinner than the chosen logical pixel pitch.

compatibility.scaling: Use a consistent logical pixel grid and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement inside the existing profile cells; preserve whole pixel clusters.
notes: Treat the display influence as a design language inside the character; exported transparency remains genuine alpha.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: Segmented LCD Game
styles.description: A mascot assembled from bold opaque LCD-like segments with characteristic gaps and mechanically limited articulation.

instructions.materials: Use opaque dark liquid-crystal-like segment shapes with a faint molded interior sheen.
instructions.forms: Build the character from linked rounded polygons and simple segmented facial symbols.
instructions.linework: Define contours by the edges of solid segments, with intentional narrow interior separations.
instructions.shading: Keep segments mostly flat; allow one restrained inner value change without glow.
instructions.palette: Use a dark dominant material with approved identity accents confined to essential markings.
instructions.texture: Suggest subtle segment surface unevenness inside shapes without a full display grid.
instructions.rendering: Render only active character segments as an isolated mascot with stable segment geometry per pose.

negative_constraints: Avoid inactive ghost segments, a rectangular screen or a display housing.
Do not insert digits, game counters or detached electronic symbols.
limitations: Segment gaps must stay large enough to survive downsampling while keeping each limb visually connected.

compatibility.scaling: Render with sufficient source detail, then downsample once with the recommended filter into the existing profile cells; inspect the final silhouette at actual size.
notes: Review interior gaps on light and dark backgrounds; extraction must not fill intended transparent separations.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: Arcade Sprite
styles.description: Energetic pixel character using exaggerated action silhouettes, strong outlines and bright clustered highlights.

instructions.materials: Use saturated opaque sprite pixels with a polished action-game finish.
instructions.forms: Exaggerate hands, feet and body lean to make each movement read instantly.
instructions.linework: Draw a bold stepped contour with thicker shadow-side clusters and clean interior separations.
instructions.shading: Place sharp two-step highlights on broad muscles, clothing or shell planes.
instructions.palette: Choose vivid approved hues balanced by a dark shared contour and bright face accents.
instructions.texture: Reserve tiny glints for a few stable locations rather than distributing sparkle noise.
instructions.rendering: Construct strong isolated key poses with consistent pixel pitch and no action-effect debris.

negative_constraints: Avoid speed trails, impact stars, projectile effects or floating score labels.
Do not trade approved facial identity for aggressive action detail.
limitations: Large poses must be designed inside the fixed safe viewport instead of shrinking individual frames.

compatibility.scaling: Use a consistent logical pixel grid and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement inside the existing profile cells; preserve whole pixel clusters.
notes: Check the widest action pose before finalizing scale; preserve one shared viewport for all arcade-style exaggeration.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: Monochrome Handheld Dots
styles.description: Single-ink character modeled through visibly ordered LCD dot clusters and intentional empty-dot highlights.

instructions.materials: Use one opaque display-ink family with explicit lit-dot clusters and unlit interior gaps.
instructions.forms: Reduce the body to compact dot-grid masses with very large facial landmarks.
instructions.linework: Keep an unbroken outer dot contour except for clearly intentional limb separations.
instructions.shading: Model light with sparse ordered empty-dot patterns inside the silhouette, not gray gradients.
instructions.palette: Use a near-monochrome ink treatment while keeping any mandatory identity color exceptions explicit.
instructions.texture: Show a regular dot rhythm in broad shaded regions and leave the face nearly solid.
instructions.rendering: Render the character-only dot structure on alpha with no colored screen rectangle.

negative_constraints: Avoid a simulated display panel, handheld casing or scanline overlay beyond the silhouette.
Do not use random holes that change the approved body contour.
limitations: If mandatory color markings carry identity, retain them explicitly and document the adapted monochrome direction.

compatibility.scaling: Use a consistent logical pixel grid and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement inside the existing profile cells; preserve whole pixel clusters.
notes: The distinct construction is an ordered display-dot lattice; the palette by itself is not a separate artistic technique.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: Limited-Palette Pixel Art
styles.description: A palette-constrained treatment of crisp pixel construction with shared color roles across the entire mascot.

instructions.materials: Use opaque pixel clusters that share a deliberate small set of color roles.
instructions.forms: Simplify the body into clearly separated masses before allocating any extra colors.
instructions.linework: Reuse one contour color across body parts and preserve uniform stepped edge rules.
instructions.shading: Share shadow and highlight colors between compatible materials instead of adding new ramps.
instructions.palette: Plan a fixed small palette covering contour, light, shade and required identity accents.
instructions.texture: Keep surfaces largely solid so scarce colors communicate anatomy rather than noise.
instructions.rendering: Render isolated pixel art with the approved palette reused exactly across every pose.

negative_constraints: Avoid inventing intermediate colors through smoothing, opacity blending or automatic gradients.
Do not discard an explicit brand color or identifying mark solely to satisfy a palette preference.
limitations: This is a compositional color treatment of pixel art and is excluded from the distinct-technique count.

compatibility.scaling: Use a consistent logical pixel grid and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement inside the existing profile cells; preserve whole pixel clusters.
notes: Validate the resulting palette after resizing; nearest-neighbor sampling preserves colors but chroma removal still needs a noncolliding key.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: Pixel Outline
styles.description: Bold stepped contour drawing around nearly empty or flat pixel interiors, emphasizing the shape of the line itself.

instructions.materials: Use solid pixel-ink bands around simple flat color body regions.
instructions.forms: Express anatomy with a broad perimeter and a few strong internal contour turns.
instructions.linework: Make a deliberate multi-pixel stepped outline the dominant visual feature throughout the figure.
instructions.shading: Restrict shading to a few flat blocks tucked beneath the outline or overlapping limbs.
instructions.palette: Separate the dark contour strongly from a small number of quiet interior colors.
instructions.texture: Keep interiors smooth and untextured so staircase line rhythm remains visible.
instructions.rendering: Draw an isolated outline-led sprite with the same line thickness on all approved poses.

negative_constraints: Avoid hairline broken contours, high-frequency interior dithering or soft outer glow.
Do not let outline thickness expand and contract accidentally from frame to frame.
limitations: Heavy contours consume interior space; faces and props need large simplified shapes.

compatibility.scaling: Use a consistent logical pixel grid and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement inside the existing profile cells; preserve whole pixel clusters.
notes: Check dark-background previews so a thick dark contour still separates clearly from the host UI.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: Retro Console Sprite
styles.description: Tile-conscious cartridge-game character with repeated modular clusters, side-readable forms and economical animation design.

instructions.materials: Use clean opaque color tiles with a graphic cartridge-game surface.
instructions.forms: Form a compact side-readable body from reusable block groups for head, torso and feet.
instructions.linework: Use rhythmic stair-step contours with repeated corner motifs across matching body parts.
instructions.shading: Shade with broad material-colored blocks that reinforce the modular construction.
instructions.palette: Share compatible ramps between limbs and clothing while preserving essential identity accents.
instructions.texture: Let repeated tile-like clusters create structure instead of fine painted texture.
instructions.rendering: Render an isolated sprite whose modular body pieces retain size and visual weight through animation.

negative_constraints: Avoid a level platform, scenery tiles or interface text accompanying the sprite.
Do not reshape repeated limb clusters inconsistently between left and right states.
limitations: Distinct asymmetrical markings must remain intentional when modular shapes are reused or mirrored.

compatibility.scaling: Use a consistent logical pixel grid and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement inside the existing profile cells; preserve whole pixel clusters.
notes: The tile influence governs drawing economy only; retain the profile atlas layout and its existing slot geometry.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.

styles.name: Hand-Painted Game Sprite
styles.description: Brush-modeled character optimized like a game asset, with broad lit planes and carefully sharpened silhouette edges.

instructions.materials: Suggest hand-painted surfaces through broad opaque brush marks tied to each material.
instructions.forms: Carve the silhouette into simple readable body masses with slightly exaggerated face and hands.
instructions.linework: Use painted contour accents at overlaps instead of a uniform ink border.
instructions.shading: Group lighting into a few large planes with soft transitions only within those planes.
instructions.palette: Keep warm and cool shifts inside a stable material palette rather than changing local colors.
instructions.texture: Place visible brush strokes on larger forms, reducing texture near eyes and fine markings.
instructions.rendering: Paint an isolated production sprite with controlled antialiased edges and one fixed light direction.

negative_constraints: Avoid concept-art scenery, atmospheric haze or a painted ground shadow.
Do not leave loose brush flecks detached from the mascot silhouette.
limitations: Subtle brush detail may disappear after downsampling; identity must depend on broad color and shape.

compatibility.scaling: Render with sufficient source detail, then downsample once with the recommended filter into the existing profile cells; inspect the final silhouette at actual size.
notes: Inspect antialiased edges against several backgrounds; prefer true alpha over keying through soft paint transitions.
Keep texture and shading inside the isolated silhouette; preserve the same approved pattern placement across animation states.
